start_with: Confirm that the installation is on Rock v16.7 or later.
Confirm that the organization received the documented development-application setup.
Inspect the Roku application record before inspecting page Lava.
Confirm that an API key is configured without exposing it.
Determine whether the failure concerns the normal Roku integration or a separate custom Lava endpoint.
If a Lava webhook is involved, review its authentication and enabled commands separately because webhook security is not provided by default.
Stop when confirming connectivity would require changing credentials or exposing a secret. Applications
branches.title: The Roku application cannot connect to Rock
branches.when: The Roku application cannot connect to Rock

start_with: Confirm that the page contains SceneGraph-oriented output rather than CMS HTML.
Confirm that `Rock:Page` is the outermost component.
Inspect Lava conditions and the available merge fields used by the page.
Check required page parameters and application context values.
Inspect page cacheability, maximum age, and maximum shared age.
If navigation supplied `rockPageCacheControl`, inspect that setting separately.
Validate the rendered result in the applicable Roku shell; a successful Lava render alone does not prove device compatibility. Pages
branches.title: A page is blank or does not render as expected
branches.when: A page is blank or does not render as expected

start_with: Confirm that the page’s outer component is `Rock:Page`.
Confirm that `initialFocus` matches the ID of a real focusable child.
Check for duplicate or missing IDs.
If a FocusGroup is used, confirm `horiz` for left/right movement or `vert` for up/down movement.
Confirm that the intended controls are children of the relevant FocusGroup.
Stop when the markup is structurally correct but device behavior has not been reproduced; record a shell/device verification gap. Page Control
branches.title: Remote focus starts nowhere or moves in the wrong direction
branches.when: Remote focus starts nowhere or moves in the wrong direction

do_not_assume: Do not assume a command chain is transactional or that all commands execute after one fails.
start_with: Confirm that the element is a supported Rock command-bearing control.
Inspect the exact `rockCommand` value.
Confirm that every required command-specific field is present.
If commands are comma-chained, test each command individually before testing the chain.
For navigation, verify the destination page identifier and optional parameters.
Do not assume a command chain is transactional or that all commands execute after one fails. Commands Button
branches.title: Selecting a button or content item does nothing
branches.when: Selecting a button or content item does nothing

start_with: Determine whether the action should push, replace, pop, or clear.
Inspect whether `pushPage` was used where `replacePage` was intended.
Inspect login or logout stack-clearing settings.
Confirm whether a command chain also changed the navigation stack.
Retest the exact route from the root page. Navigation
branches.title: Back navigation returns to the wrong screen
branches.when: Back navigation returns to the wrong screen

do_not_assume: Do not claim resolution until the behavior is retested across the relevant anonymous and authenticated states.
start_with: Inspect the page’s cacheability type.
Inspect Max Age and Max Shared Age.
Inspect navigation-level `rockPageCacheControl`.
Determine whether a personalized request should use personal or private caching rather than public caching.
Inspect whether the navigation stack was cleared after login or logout.
Confirm the current person and context values used by the page.
Do not claim resolution until the behavior is retested across the relevant anonymous and authenticated states. Pages Navigation
branches.title: Personalized content is stale or appears for the wrong person
branches.when: Personalized content is stale or appears for the wrong person

start_with: Confirm that the application record references a website authentication page.
Confirm that the login command points to a Roku login page.
Confirm that the page contains `lgnQrPoster` and `lgnCodeLabel`.
Inspect timeout, polling, success-page, and timeout-page settings.
Confirm that the success and timeout destinations exist.
Test the website authentication page independently.
Stop when further testing requires changing authentication configuration or using a real account without authorization. Applications
branches.title: The QR login flow does not complete
branches.when: The QR login flow does not complete

start_with: Reject YouTube URLs for this command path.
Confirm that video is a directly playable MP4 or HLS resource, or that audio is an MP3 resource.
Confirm that the Roku device can reach the URL.
Inspect the correct command-specific URL field.
If the content is live, inspect the live-stream flag.
If a Rock Media Element is involved, inspect the media-element association.
Treat format, hosting, authorization, and device reachability as separate checks.
branches.title: Video or audio does not play
branches.when: Video or audio does not play

start_with: Confirm that `rockWatchMap` is present.
Confirm that the prior `rockInteractionGuid` is also present.
If only the watch map was supplied, expect resume behavior with a new interaction and fresh watch map.
Confirm that the supplied interaction belongs to the intended playback history.
Verify the resulting tracking behavior rather than inferring it from the command markup.
branches.title: Playback resumes but creates a new interaction
branches.when: Playback resumes but creates a new interaction

start_with: Confirm that the RowList has one root ContentNode assigned to the `content` role.
Confirm that each row is represented by a child ContentNode.
Confirm that each row contains item ContentNodes.
Inspect row titles and item `hdposterurl` values when used.
Only after validating the hierarchy, inspect sizes, spacing, visible-row count, and focus-animation settings.
branches.title: A RowList has no rows or items
branches.when: A RowList has no rows or items

entrypoint: Choose the branch whose symptom matches the user's task, then inspect the live records before making changes.
